title: Potential Reinforcement of Health Misconceptions in YouTube Videos: Example of Elbow Enthesopathy (Tennis Elbow)
screen_reason: Abstract-only text, but it reports a complete quantitative share with a denominator: “Sixty-five percent (91 of 139) of videos contained information reinforcing at least one common misconception regarding eECRB.” The denominator is all videos retrieved for two search terms (items that exist), so the construct is CONTENT — a share of items conveying inaccurate/misleading health content. Coded borderline because the numerator is “potential reinforcement of a misconception / unhelpful thinking” assessed with an author-designed rubric rather than a verbatim false-claim judgement, and a factually accurate video could conceivably receive the label (see notes for the QUALITY reading).

estimates.moderator_quote: METHODS: We recorded video metric data on 139 unique YouTube videos when searching "lateral epicondylitis" and "tennis elbow."
estimates.notes: ADJUDICATOR NOTE — construct call. I coded CONTENT because the label is “reinforcing a common misconception”, i.e. content conveying a false belief about a health condition, which falls inside this review's broad definition (“inaccurate or misleading (health) content”). The competing reading is QUALITY: the rubric measures “potential reinforcement of unhelpful thinking”, which is hedged (potential) and belief-framing rather than claim falsity, so a factually accurate video could in principle be scored as reinforcing a misconception — the §3 test “if a wholly true item could receive the label, it is QUALITY”. The authors themselves treat misconception-reinforcement as distinct from informational quality (DISCERN scored separately, with no factors associated), which is the main reason I did not collapse it into QUALITY. borderline=true either way. FIELD GAPS (abstract-only): no data-collection date and no publication year appear in the text, so year is left empty rather than guessed; whether the 139 videos were a rank-truncated set (which would make denom_selection=curated) is not stated, so denom_selection is left blank; no country is given.

missed_or_uncertain: Abstract-only text, so nothing beyond the single headline share could be extracted. Seen but not extractable: the adapted DISCERN informational-quality scores (no share, no distribution reported in the abstract — a QUALITY row cannot be built without a value); the associations of misconception-reinforcement with video duration, likes per day and likes per view (associations, not shares); the “level” of reinforcement, which the rubric apparently graded but which is reported only dichotomously (“at least one”) in the abstract. Full text would be needed for: data-collection date, publication year, number and qualifications of coders, inter-rater reliability, whether the video set was rank-truncated, and any stricter definition variant (e.g. share of videos reinforcing multiple misconceptions).

rob.design: Cross-sectional YouTube content analysis of 139 unique videos retrieved with the searches “lateral epicondylitis” and “tennis elbow”; video metric data recorded; an author-designed rubric scored the level of potential reinforcement of unhelpful thinking, and informational quality was scored with an adapted DISCERN instrument; factors associated with the scores were then assessed. No sampling method beyond the two search terms, no coder count, no response-rate concept, and no reliability statistics are reported in the abstract-only text available.
